records.title: Dewi Siluman Ular
records.meta: Film · Indonesia · Indonesian · horror · directed by Azhar Kinoi Lubis · produced by Starvision / Chand Parwez Servia · written by Upi and Ayu Anggraini Putri · theatrical release 12 Nov 2026 · starring Derby Romero, Anya Geraldine, Aulia Sarah and Aghniny Haque · adapted from the podcast 'Nikah Sama Jin'
records.character: Rahma (Dedi's first wife, about to undergo a caesarean); Dewi (a jinn in the form of a snake spirit, whom Dedi marries)
records.summary: Bakery owner Dedi is being chased by debt collectors while his wife Rahma needs a caesarean. Desperate to save her and their unborn child, he makes a pesugihan pact and marries Dewi, a snake-spirit jinn. The choice brings terror on the household, which also includes a third wife, Lela.
records.hypnotist: Dewi (snake-spirit jinn), bound by a pesugihan marriage pact
records.method: Pesugihan ritual / marriage to a jinn
records.evidence: Two independent Indonesian press synopses: Dedi marries the snake-spirit Dewi to fund his pregnant wife Rahma's caesarean; a third wife, Lela, is also named. Theatrical date is 12 Nov 2026.
records.pregnancy_note: The pact is made by the husband, not a woman bargaining for a pregnancy; Rahma is already pregnant. Partner in the household: Dedi. Dewi is presented as a jinn/spirit wife.

records.title: Fruit (Buah)
records.meta: Short film · Singapore · Malay · 15 min · directed by Jen Nee Lim · starring Tysha Khan as Siti and Wan Ahmad as her husband · 2026 Sundance Film Festival (Short Film Program 2) · later awarded at Clermont-Ferrand
records.character: Siti (a married woman who has just discovered she is pregnant and does not want the child)
records.summary: Set in a time when abortion is illegal, Siti does not want to continue her pregnancy. After ordinary attempts to end it fail, she encounters a Pontianak — a Southeast Asian childbirth spirit usually said to prey on men and pregnant women — reimagined here as a liberator who helps her escape an unwanted pregnancy.
records.hypnotist: A Pontianak, recast as a helper rather than a predator
records.method: Encounter with a childbirth spirit from Malay folklore
records.evidence: Two independent interviews/features (Park Record at Sundance; Voilah! after Clermont-Ferrand) describe Siti as a wife who does not want her pregnancy and a Pontianak who helps her. The articles do not spell out the final outcome.
records.pregnancy_note: Partner in the household: her husband, who unlike Siti wants the child. The film is about bodily autonomy and a revised Pontianak myth, not a sex scene and not conception-only.

records.title: Forbidden Fruits
records.meta: Film · United States · English · horror comedy · R-rated · 103 min · written by Meredith Alloway and Lily Houghton · directed by Meredith Alloway · theatrical release 27 Mar 2026 · starring Lili Reinhart, Lola Tung, Victoria Pedretti and Alexandra Shipp · world premiere at SXSW
records.character: Apple (leader of the coven, played by Lili Reinhart); Cherry, Fig, and new hire Pumpkin (coworkers drawn into the group)
records.summary: At a Dallas mall boutique called Free Eden, saleswoman Apple leads a secret witch coven with coworkers Cherry and Fig. New hire Pumpkin is brought into their tightly ruled sisterhood, comes to believe something supernatural is at work, and the group's curses and internal power struggle turn violent.
records.hypnotist: Apple, as leader of the coven
records.evidence: The official synopsis and a full RogerEbert.com review both describe an adult workplace coven: Apple subjugates the others to the group's rules, they curse people who afflict them, and the conflict turns violent. The review is filed from the SXSW premiere; the theatrical date is 27 Mar 2026.
